news_summary: A London housing project has been recognized for excellence by winning a prestigious architecture award.
news_summary_fr: Un projet immobilier londonien a été récompensé pour son excellence en remportant un prestigieux prix d'architecture.
news_summary_es: Un proyecto de viviendas en Londres ha sido reconocido por su excelencia al ganar un prestigioso premio de arquitectura.

articles.title: London housing project wins top architecture award
articles.summary: Lion Green Road in Coulsdon was recognised for the way it responds to its surroundings.
articles.content:
Williamson told the BBC that until he went to study architecture he lived in a council estate in the East Midlands, "and every time I go back there all the council houses have been sold off, they're in private hands.

"Which in a way can be a good thing - we're in a homeowning democracy - but the sad thing is they haven't been replaced.

"Every time I go back - without getting too emotional - I think 'where would we have lived?'

"So to me that's why this particular project was important. I think a lot of people from that sort of background live in terrible accommodation - temporary accommodation which isn't safe or secure.

"These houses are fantastic and they're part of a mixed scheme so it's got a fantastic feel to it.

"For me it was a very inspirational, emotional, part of the process."

Duggan, who was brought up in south-west London, said the scheme "challenged conventional suburban housing layouts centred on roads, private gardens and clearly defined front and back spaces".

Winding paths and planting weave between the blocks, connecting them and linking shared outdoor spaces.

She said she wanted it to be a public space people felt they could belong to.

"Housing needs to be progressive. People who live in the building have access to green space, allotments."

The site fronts onto Lion Green Road, with low-rise green belt housing set on higher ground to the south and traditional suburban streets to the north.
articles.reasoning: The article highlights a housing project recognized for its innovative, community-focused design that improves living conditions and public space access, addressing broader social housing challenges and promoting inclusive, progressive housing solutions.
articles.personality_title: London housing project wins top architecture award for community design
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – A new housing project in Coulsdon, South London, called Lion Green Road, has been noticed for its special design that fits well with the area around it. The project was created to offer better homes and shared spaces for people, especially those who might have had difficult housing before.

**What happened** – The Lion Green Road housing project recently won a major architecture award. The designers focused on creating homes that feel safe, welcoming, and connected to nature. Instead of the usual straight roads and separate gardens, the project features winding paths and shared green spaces where residents can meet and enjoy the outdoors together.

**Impact** – This project is important because it offers a new way to think about housing. It moves away from typical suburban layouts and creates a community where people can feel they belong. The design includes green spaces and areas for growing plants, which improve life for the people living there. It also responds to a problem where many council houses have been sold but not replaced, leaving some people without secure homes.

**What's next step** – The success of Lion Green Road might inspire other housing projects to focus more on community and green spaces. Architects and city planners could use these ideas to build better, safer neighborhoods in other places, helping more people find good homes.

**One-sentence takeaway** – The Lion Green Road housing project shows how thoughtful design can create safer, greener, and more connected communities in cities.
articles.personality_title_fr: Un projet de logement à Londres récompensé pour son design communautaire
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Un nouveau projet de logements à Coulsdon, dans le sud de Londres, appelé Lion Green Road, a été reconnu pour son design qui s’intègre bien à son environnement. Ce projet vise à offrir de meilleurs logements et des espaces partagés aux habitants, notamment ceux qui avaient auparavant des conditions difficiles.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Le projet de logements Lion Green Road a récemment remporté un grand prix d’architecture. Les concepteurs ont créé des maisons sûres, accueillantes, et connectées à la nature. Au lieu des rues droites et des jardins séparés habituels, le projet propose des chemins sinueux et des espaces verts partagés où les habitants peuvent se rencontrer et profiter ensemble de l’extérieur.

**Impact** – Ce projet est important car il propose une nouvelle façon de penser le logement. Il s’éloigne des plans suburbains classiques pour créer une communauté où les gens peuvent se sentir chez eux. Le design inclut des espaces verts et des zones pour cultiver des plantes, ce qui améliore la vie des habitants. Il répond aussi à un problème où beaucoup de logements sociaux ont été vendus sans être remplacés, laissant certaines personnes sans maison sûre.

**Prochaine étape** – Le succès de Lion Green Road pourrait inspirer d’autres projets de logements à se concentrer davantage sur la communauté et les espaces verts. Les architectes et urbanistes pourraient utiliser ces idées pour construire de meilleurs quartiers, offrant ainsi de bons logements à plus de personnes.

**Conclusion en une phrase** – Le projet de logements Lion Green Road montre comment un design réfléchi peut créer des communautés plus sûres, plus vertes, et plus unies en ville.
articles.personality_title_es: Proyecto de viviendas en Londres gana premio por diseño comunitario
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Un nuevo proyecto de viviendas en Coulsdon, al sur de Londres, llamado Lion Green Road, ha sido reconocido por su diseño que se adapta bien al entorno. El proyecto busca ofrecer mejores hogares y espacios compartidos para las personas, especialmente para quienes antes tenían condiciones difíciles.

**Qué pasó** – El proyecto de viviendas Lion Green Road ganó recientemente un importante premio de arquitectura. Los diseñadores crearon casas seguras, acogedoras y conectadas con la naturaleza. En lugar de las calles rectas y jardines separados comunes, el proyecto tiene caminos sinuosos y espacios verdes compartidos donde los vecinos pueden reunirse y disfrutar del aire libre juntos.

**Impacto** – Este proyecto es importante porque ofrece una nueva forma de pensar la vivienda. Se aleja de los diseños suburbanos tradicionales y crea una comunidad donde las personas pueden sentirse parte. El diseño incluye espacios verdes y áreas para cultivar plantas, mejorando la vida de quienes viven allí. También responde a un problema donde muchas casas públicas fueron vendidas sin ser reemplazadas, dejando a algunas personas sin hogares seguros.

**Próximo paso** – El éxito de Lion Green Road podría inspirar a otros proyectos de viviendas a enfocarse más en la comunidad y los espacios verdes. Arquitectos y planificadores podrían usar estas ideas para construir vecindarios mejores y más seguros en otros lugares, ayudando a más personas a tener buenos hogares.

**Conclusión en una frase** – El proyecto de viviendas Lion Green Road demuestra cómo un diseño cuidadoso puede crear comunidades urbanas más seguras, verdes y conectadas.
